concerns.text: Task T017 (runner.py) is marked as depending on T053 and T055 (memory optimizations), but T017 is listed BEFORE T053/T055 in the task sequence. A consumer (T017) cannot precede its producers (T053/T055). T017 must be moved after T053/T055.

Task T017 depends on T053/T055, but T053/T055 are marked [P] (parallel-safe) and placed in the same phase. If T017 is a blocking dependency for US2/US3, the memory optimization tasks (T053-T055) must be completed and verified BEFORE T017 can run. The current ordering implies T017 runs before the memory fixes are applied, violating the 'Producer before Consumer' rule.

Task T034 (N > 50 edge case) is listed after T033 (runner integration). However, T033 requires the runner to handle N=50 and memory constraints. If T034 implements the degradation logic required for N>50 (FR-016), it should ideally precede or be part of the foundational runner implementation (T033) to ensure the runner is robust before integration. More critically, T034b (test for T034) depends on T034, but T034 is listed after T033 which might already assume the logic exists.

Task T052b (Noise Correlation Sweep) depends on T036 (correlation support in MDP). T036 is listed after T035 (logging). While T036 is in the same phase, T052b is listed at the very end. The dependency chain is valid, but T036 should be grouped with T031/T032 (MDP/Heuristic verification) to ensure the MDP supports correlation before the runner (T033) or analysis (T035) attempts to use it. Currently, T033 (runner) might run before T036 (correlation support) is implemented, causing runtime errors if correlation is passed.

Task T014 (defaults.yaml) is marked [P] and placed in Phase 2. However, T015 (synthetic_mdp.py) and T016 (heuristic.py) likely depend on the config values defined in T014. While T014 is listed first, the [P] tag implies it can run in parallel with T015/T016. If T015/T016 read from T014 at runtime, this is fine, but if they read at import/compile time or during task execution setup, T014 must strictly precede them. The [P] tag is risky here if the config is a hard dependency for the module initialization.
